title: SHAP explainer artifacts are pickle-based; keep docs and nested-model serialization in sync
answers: Is a SHAP explainer artifact pickle-free?
Can I use skops to make SHAP explainers safe to load?
Is load_explainer safe for untrusted sources?
How do I stop SHAP explainers loading outside Databricks with pickle disabled?
body:
Invariant: A SHAP explainer artifact is always pickle-based, because the explainer state uses pickle regardless of serialize_model_using_mlflow. Making only the nested sklearn model skops-only or auto-trusting skops-rejected types does not make the full artifact pickle-free or safe for untrusted sources.
Enforced in: mlflow/shap/__init__.py:save_explainer (nested sklearn uses cloudpickle) and load_explainer (docstring warning to load only trusted sources).
What breaks if skipped: Docs or docstrings that call SHAP artifacts pickle-free mislead users into loading untrusted files. MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false blocks SHAP loads outside Databricks Runtime and Model Serving.
Keep in sync: the serialize_model_using_mlflow docstrings in log_explainer and save_explainer, the load_explainer warning, and the 'SHAP explainers remain pickle-based' section of the pickle-free models guide.
applies: Any change to SHAP explainer serialization, its docstrings, or the pickle-free models guide. Standalone mlflow.sklearn models are not covered.
says: Documentation claims model explainers are safe to load from untrusted sources.
Loading saved model explainers fails when untrusted model serialization is blocked in our environment.
Add a security warning that model explainers should only be opened from trusted authors.
Clarify in the security documentation that saved explainers still rely on unsafe serialization formats.
Explainability artifacts cannot be loaded in external environments when insecure deserialization is turned off.
search: SHAP explainer artifacts remain pickle-based regardless of `serialize_model_using_mlflow` because the explainer state itself uses pickle, meaning artifacts are never safe for untrusted sources. In `mlflow/shap/__init__.py`, `save_explainer` serializes nested scikit-learn models using cloudpickle, while `load_explainer` docstrings must warn users to load only trusted files. Disabling pickle via `MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false` blocks loading SHAP explainers outside Databricks Runtime and Model Serving. Applies to SHAP explainer serialization, docstrings, and `docs/docs/classic-ml/tracking/pickle-free-models/index.mdx`, but does not cover standalone `mlflow.sklearn` models.
